searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent. Searches restricted to seifried.co.nz, greenhough.co.nz, kahurangiwine.com and rimugrove.co.nz are read as the house through their summaries. Several searches blocked the author's own sources so the second source would be independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or hedged.
Writers' own sites (Wine Anorak, Wine With Seth, Raymond Chan, Cameron Douglas) met among the results are not cited; the author's Wine Anorak source was replaced.

tested: 1976 move to an ex-commune property and 1978 planting: house, New Zealand Wine, JNW. Sound.
Mendoza clone, firm acid and high extract: the house's product page and The Real Review. Sound.
Home Block among the first Chardonnay of the South Island: only as one of the oldest commercial vineyards, in the importer and the house. Hedged.
Making: the house's sheet of 2022 and 2023: native yeast, high solids, about 15 per cent new oak, ten months full lees stirred monthly, three months fine lees in steel. Sound, sharpened.
Rosie's Block: bought in 1999, from another family, by several importers; one says planted. Changed.
Amphora Chardonnay from Rosie's Block: Decanter and a merchant. Sound.
Ageing: reviews and merchants, five to fifteen years. Rewritten.

changes.now: the founders no longer said to come from the North Island, which no source read gives.
among the first Chardonnay of the South Island now by the house's account among the oldest commercial Chardonnay vineyards of the South Island, as the importer and the house say it.
Rosie's Block was bought in 1999, not planted then (importers and Decanter's notes).
the closing claim of a first now says the white carried the name of the Moutere hills into New Zealand Chardonnay.
about a sixth of the oak new in the 2022 to 2024 vintages and monthly stirring, from the house's sheet and The Real Review.
five to ten years for most vintages, older bottles well past a decade, from reviews in place of the author's reading.
Wine Anorak and the Cellars note replaced by JNW and The Real Review (a writer's own site is no source).

open: Neudorf's Home Block as among the oldest Chardonnay of the South Island rests on the house and its importer only.

tested: 1971 arrival, Southland, 1973 planting, 1976 first vintage: the house, New Zealand Wine, Nelson Weekly. Sound.
Came to make apple wine for the Apple and Pear Board: Nelson Weekly. Added.
Too cold warnings: sources say advisers doubted the South Island suited wine. Changed.
Redwood Valley 1979: the house's vineyard page; Taste Nelson gives a purchase of 1982. Hedged.
Kahurangi 1998: Taste Nelson and Top Tastes. Sound.
Raisined without botrytis: the house's notes of 2008 to 2024 and a Norwegian importer; a critic once read the 2008 as freeze concentrated. Sound, question distractor changed.
Fermentation about three weeks, bottled within the year, none in 2020: the house's notes. Sharpened.
DWWA 2014 regional trophy for the 2012: Decanter and the house. Sound.

changes.now: the founder came to Nelson in 1971 to make apple wine for the New Zealand Apple and Pear Board (Nelson Weekly and the house).
the warnings that Nelson was too cold became the doubts of many, government farm advisers among them, that the South Island suited wine, as the sources say it.
Redwood Valley planted in 1979 now by the family's account (Taste Nelson gives a purchase of 1982); its oldest vines claim cut.
fermentation of two and a half to three weeks and no wine in 2020, from the house's vintage notes.
the distractor of frozen juice replaced, since one critic once read the 2008 as freeze concentrated; explanation rewritten.
the British importer's page replaced by Taste Nelson's history.

open: A critic's review of 2010 described the 2008 as freeze concentrated; the house's own 2008 notes say raisined on the vine. The record follows the house.

tested: Late 1990 move from Auckland, an established vineyard: New Zealand Wine, Curious Wines. Sound, sharpened.
Organic from 2008, BioGro 2011: two sources and the house. Sound.
Clones UCD5 and AM 10/5 of 1993: the house only, hedged as its account. Sound.
Wild yeast for the Pinot Noir: no source. Cut.
Unfined and unfiltered: the 2014 sheet says egg white fined and filtered; the house's 2023 page unfined and lightly filtered. Changed, and the wine question replaced.
Whole bunches only lately in the style: the house's 2023 page. Sharpened.

changes.now: wild yeast and few punch downs cut, no source for the Pinot Noir; whole bunches told as of the 2020s and lately joined the style, by the house's 2023 page; ten months to a year in barrique.
bottled without fining or filtration was wrong for some years: the 2014 was fined with egg white and filtered, the 2023 unfined and lightly filtered.
wild fermented and bottled unfined replaced by small open fermenters with a share of whole bunches.
the couple took on an established vineyard in late 1990 (New Zealand Wine, Curious Wines).
replaced, since its key and a distractor turned on fining and filtration that changed by vintage; it now asks the clones of 1993.
Glengarry and Vino Fino replaced by New Zealand Wine's winery page and the 2014 sheet.

open: The drinking window, most vintages within a decade, rests on one review and the author's reading.
Who first planted the vineyard before 1990 is not told for want of a second source.

tested: 1998 establishment on the original Seifried site: Taste Nelson, Top Tastes. Sound.
Oldest commercial Riesling of the South Island: the house's own pages and a regional guide; hedged as the house's.

Heaphy as a rival claimant: wrong framing. The same couple founded both; Heaphy's winery is on Sunrise Road and its Moutere Old Vine Riesling comes from blocks Hermann Seifried planted in the early 1970s (Boutinot, New Zealand Wine). Changed.
The vineyard and winery offered for sale and lease back in 2017, the business later sold in parts: a newspaper and Top Tastes. Left open, not told.
Grapes of the home block, Montepulciano among them: not shown to be from the block. Cut.

changes.now: Sunrise Road dropped as the house's address: Heaphy's winery stands on Sunrise Road, and where Kahurangi makes its wine today is not settled.
the warnings that Nelson was too cold became doubts that the South Island suited wine.
the list of grapes of the home block cut (Montepulciano is a Regional Selection wine, not shown to be from the block).
Heaphy is no rival neighbour: the couple who founded Kahurangi Estate also founded Heaphy, whose old vine Riesling comes from early Seifried plantings at Sunrise Road (Taste Nelson, Boutinot).
the unsourced praise of reviewers cut.
1979 Redwood Valley replaced by 1976 the first Seifried vintage.
Glengarry and the Seifried story replaced by Boutinot's Heaphy page and Taste Nelson's report of the Heaphy sale.

open: Kahurangi's own pages still claim the 1973 vines for its Riesling while Heaphy's Moutere Old Vine Riesling claims the same oldest block; the founders sold the vineyard (offered for sale and lease back in 2017) and later Heaphy. Whether today's Kahurangi Estate Riesling still comes from the vines of 1973 is not settled: the integrator should weigh a swap to Heaphy's Moutere Old Vine Riesling.
Heaphy's own importer gives 1970 on one page and 1973 on another for its oldest Riesling block.

tested: 1995 purchase and planting by a Californian on the north facing Bronte Peninsula: Taste Nelson, Wine Nelson, a Nelson Mail profile, the house. Sound.
Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris planted: the house. Sound.
Former orchard: no source. Cut.
Cold soak five to seven days, open vats plunged three times a day: the house's notes of 2003 to 2009. Sharpened.
Unfined and unfiltered: only the 2009; the 2004 and 2005 coarse filtered. Changed.
First wine 2000: the Nelson Mail profile and the house's back vintages. Added.

changes.now: the former orchard cut, no source.
cold soak of five to seven days and plunging three times a day from the house's vintage notes; bottled without fining or filtration was wrong for some years: the 2004 and 2005 were coarse filtered.
bottled unfined replaced by cold soaked and plunged by hand.
the founder a Californian, and the first wine of 2000 (Taste Nelson, Top Tastes, the house's back vintages).
now asks the cold soak, not the filtration.
the orchard taken out of the stem.
Grape to Glass replaced by Taste Nelson's page on the winery.

open: The first wine of 2000 rests on a regional profile and the house's back vintages reaching to 2000.

livingNamesMet: Neudorf: Judy Finn (founder), Rosie Finn, Todd Stevens (winemaker); Tim Finn reported dead in 2024 in one source, so not named.
Seifried: Hermann and Agnes Seifried (founders; Agnes stands only as the label's Sweet Agnes).
Kahurangi and Heaphy: Greg and Amanda Day; Hadyn Ellis (a director).
Rimu Grove: Patrick Stowe, Barbara Dunn.
Critics met in results: Jamie Goode, Raymond Chan, Cameron Douglas.
None is named in the fragment; the read-together agent may add them to people.json.

swaps.proposed: house: Rimu Grove to Waimea Estates or Mahana
swaps.why: The core facts of Rimu Grove (1995, the Bronte Peninsula, a Californian founder, Pinot Noir from its own vines, the first wine of 2000) now stand on the house and two regional sources, and the thin region rule allows a small estate told plainly as one. No replacement record was written or refuted in this run.

swaps.proposed: wine: Kahurangi Estate Riesling to Mt Arthur Reserve Riesling (noted by the author, not proposed)
swaps.why: No second source makes the reserve the house's flagship. A different question is raised instead in the record's open list: whether the old vines of 1973 now belong to Heaphy, whose Moutere Old Vine Riesling may be the truer pick for the site.

codexTension: The region summary says the first modern vines went in at Upper Moutere in 1973 and Neudorf's Moutere Chardonnay carried the name since the 1980s: consistent, though the first vintage of 1981 rests on one writer's site.
The region record's producers line for Neudorf says the wine gave Nelson a place among the country's best: a ranking this record does not repeat (author's report).
The plan's why for Greenhough gives 1991; the sources give late 1990 for the move and the record leaves founded empty.
The plan's why for Seifried calls Sweet Agnes first released in 2006 on one importer's sheet only; the record gives no year.
The plan's why and the region record tell Kahurangi's Riesling as from the 1973 vines; Heaphy now claims the same block.
